tax_compliance.title: Accounts 5 — Tax Accounting & Nigerian Compliance
tax_compliance.desc: The money-heavy module: the custody thesis consolidated, the Nigerian frame at consultant altitude, VAT both sides in one position, WHT both directions, PAYE and the payroll custodies, the six-step filing ritual and zeroing invariant, the compliance calendar and reserve, and the audit evidence posture.

lessons.title: Chapter 1 — The silent partner: custody consolidated
lessons.html:
Three tracks met the tax accounts one at a time — output VAT at the invoice (Selling 6), input VAT and WHT at the bill (Procurement 7), PAYE at the payroll journal (module 2). This module consolidates them into what they jointly are: the state's wallet inside the firm's chart — and the discipline of a firm that holds another party's money professionally.

The custody thesis, stated once for everything. Tax money in a trading firm is overwhelmingly money the firm HOLDS, not money it OWES from its own pocket: the VAT charged on every invoice was collected FROM customers FOR the state; the WHT deducted from a supplier's payment is the supplier's tax, held in transit; PAYE is the employees' income tax, withheld at source. The grammar makes it visible (these are all CREDITS to liability accounts — module 1's ₦7,500 line), and the operational consequence is the module's spine: custody money is not revenue, not cash flow, and not available — the firm that treats its VAT account as working capital is spending someone else's money, and remittance day arrives as a crisis precisely as often as that treatment is habitual. Chapter 7's reserve discipline is the cure; this chapter's job is that the disease is understood as what it is.

The wallet's compartments. The custody and near-custody accounts a trading firm carries: VAT Payable (output custody) and Input VAT (the claimable asset that offsets it — Chapter 3 joins them); WHT Payable (custody as deducting agent) and WHT Receivable (the mirror — the firm's OWN tax prepaid via customers' deductions, an asset with a chase attached — Chapter 4); the payroll custodies (PAYE, pension, and the statutory family — Chapter 5); and beside them the firm's own tax liabilities proper (companies income tax and its kin — provision-style accounts the accountant owns, distinguished exactly because they ARE the firm's own cost, not custody). Every compartment is an account (module 1's types), fed by documents and templates (the posting map), reconciled to a register, and cleared by a remittance ritual — one pattern, five appearances, which is why one module can hold them all.

Compliance as rhythm, not emergency. The module's cultural argument, previewed: Nigerian tax compliance for a documented trading firm is a CALENDAR — monthly returns and remittances on fixed days, annual filings on fixed horizons, each fed by registers the system already keeps. The firm that experiences compliance as recurring emergency has not met a harsher authority than its neighbours; it has declined the rhythm — filings reconstructed from spreadsheets at deadline, custody money discovered spent, certificates never collected. The consultant's product in this module is the boring version: registers that tie, accounts that zero, a calendar with names, and an evidence file that answers queries in a day (Chapter 8). Boring, as three tracks have established, is the certificate.

lessons.title: Chapter 2 — The Nigerian frame: the landscape, for consultants
lessons.html:
The machinery is universal; the landscape is Nigerian — and a consultant implementing for Nigerian trading firms needs the map at working altitude: what taxes touch the client, who collects them, what the 2025 reform reshaped, and where the consultant's competence ends. This chapter is that map — deliberately conceptual, because rates and thresholds are the accountant's living knowledge, not a manual's frozen table.

The taxes that touch a trading firm. The working set: VAT — the consumption tax on supplies, collected and remitted monthly (Chapter 3); WHT — the withholding mechanism riding specified payment types, both directions (Chapter 4); PAYE — employees' income tax withheld monthly, remitted to the STATE authority of the employee's residence (the federal/state split that surprises new consultants: VAT and companies income tax run federal; PAYE runs to states — one firm, several authorities, one calendar); Companies Income Tax — the firm's own annual tax on profits, provisioned through the year and the accountant's core territory; and the statutory family around payroll (pension, housing, insurance, training levies — Chapter 5's concepts). Each has its authority, its rhythm, and its account — and the consultant's competence is knowing WHICH machinery serves each, not computing any of them.

The 2025 reform, at consultant altitude. The Nigeria Tax Act 2025 and its companion acts consolidated a scattered statute book and restructured administration — the working consequences a consultant should hold: the tax authority landscape reorganised (the federal service restructured under new legislation, with the system's registrations and filing rails updated accordingly), thresholds and reliefs reshaped (small-company regimes, rate structures, and exemption bands moved — the accountant re-reads eligibility annually, and the consultant's contribution is that the system can APPLY whatever the current answer is: templates adjustable, categories flaggable), and the compliance infrastructure pushed further digital — e-filing as the norm, and e-invoicing/fiscalisation advancing (Selling 6 taught the merchant-facing reality; the accounts chair's addition is that the invoice register and the filed return increasingly reconcile AUTOMATICALLY on the authority's side — which converts register-to-account discipline from good practice into survival, because the authority now holds one half of the reconciliation).

The consultant's boundary, drawn once for the module. The Inventory 5 boundary, tax edition, and it governs every chapter ahead: the machinery is yours; the advice is theirs. Yours: the templates that compute correctly, the registers that tie to accounts, the rituals and calendar installed, the evidence file structured, the system's categories able to express whatever treatment the accountant directs. Theirs: what rate applies to this transaction, whether this firm qualifies for that regime, how this deduction interacts with that relief, what position to take when the law is unclear. The consultant who answers rate-and-eligibility questions is practising tax without a licence and assuming liability without insurance; the one who says the system can do whichever your tax adviser directs — here is how is doing the job at its professional grade. This sentence recurs because clients will test it monthly.

lessons.title: Chapter 3 — VAT consolidated: both sides, one position
lessons.html:
Two tracks each held half; the accounts chair holds the whole: output and input joined into the monthly VAT position, and the ritual that files it. The consolidation chapter.

The two sides, recapped in one breath. OUTPUT (Selling 6): every taxable sale charges VAT via the template — CR VAT Payable, the custody growing with trade, the invoice register its document-level mirror. INPUT (Procurement 7): VAT paid on qualifying purchases — DR Input VAT, an asset, the claim's evidence being the supplier's proper invoice (the discipline that made invoice quality a money issue: ₦100-with-input beats ₦99-without). The chart carries both compartments (module 1's typed accounts), the documents feed both automatically, and the chair's monthly work is joining them.

The net position. The month's arithmetic: output charged minus allowable input equals the position — PAYABLE when output exceeds input (the normal trading month: remit the net), a CARRY-FORWARD credit when input exceeds output (the heavy-buying month, the import-stocking quarter — the credit rides to offset future output, with refund mechanics existing in principle but carry-forward being the practical road). The system computes it because the documents fed it; the return states it; and the reconciliation BEFORE filing is the ritual's heart: the invoice register's output total ties to the VAT Payable account's movement; the purchase register's input total ties to the Input VAT account's movement — the two register-to-account bridges both money tracks installed, now run as one pre-filing checklist line, because a return filed from numbers the ledger cannot reproduce is Chapter 10's pattern wearing a stamp.

The classification edges. Where VAT literacy earns its keep — the categories the templates must express: standard-rated supplies (the default trading reality), zero-rated (taxable at zero — the distinction that matters because zero-rated supplies still belong in the return and preserve input claims on their costs), exempt (outside the charge — and the subtle consequence the accountant will care about: input VAT attributable to exempt supplies is generally not claimable, so a mixed-supply firm — the pharmacy whose basic-medicine lines ride an exemption while its cosmetics shelf is standard-rated — needs its ITEMS tax-categorised correctly at the master level so the registers can tell the streams apart; the apportionment arithmetic is the accountant's, the categorisation machinery is yours), and the special regimes the accountant flags (imports' VAT at clearing — Procurement 6's landed file; reverse-charge concepts on certain imported services). The item-master tax category is where all of this becomes operational — one more master-data field with a decade of consequences, set at creation, audited annually.

The monthly VAT ritual, end to end. Register closed for the month (both sides); registers reconciled to accounts (the two bridges, to the kobo, divergences worked before — never after — filing); the return prepared FROM the system's numbers (the return is a restatement of the ledger, not a parallel computation); filed by the calendar's date; the net remitted; and the accounts cleared — the payment entry that empties VAT Payable (net of the input offset) against the bank, leaving the custody at its post-remittance level (zero, or the carry-forward, exactly). The invariant Chapter 6 generalises debuts here: after a clean cycle, the custody account's balance is explainable in one sentence — and any residue that isn't is next month's first worked item.

lessons.title: Chapter 4 — WHT both directions: agent and sufferer
lessons.html:
Withholding tax is the mechanism trading firms most often hold wrong, because it runs in BOTH directions at once and each direction has a different accounting life. The chair's consolidated treatment.

As agent: deducting from suppliers. Procurement 7's machinery, recapped as custody: qualifying payments (services, rent, professional fees, contracts — the TYPES are set by law; the current rates and thresholds are the accountant's living table) are settled net, the deduction credited to WHT Payable — the supplier's tax, held: the ₦1m professional invoice settled as ₦950k cash plus ₦50k custody. The agent's obligations complete the picture: the custody REMITTED monthly by the calendar (Chapter 6's ritual — the account zeroing after), and the certificates procured and delivered to the suppliers whose money was withheld — because the certificate is the supplier's evidence for THEIR tax credit, and the agent who deducts but never delivers certificates is quietly injuring every supplier it pays (the relationship cost) while accumulating an administrative debt (the compliance cost). The deduction-detail register — who, what, when, how much — is the remittance schedule's source and the certificate run's checklist, one register serving both.

As sufferer: customers deducting from you. The mirror, and the direction firms neglect at real cost: corporate and government customers deduct WHT from THEIR payments to the firm — the ₦1m receivable settling as ₦950k cash plus a ₦50k deduction. The accounting: the deduction is NOT a discount, a loss, or a mystery shortpay (Chapter 2 of module 4's taxonomy at work) — it is the firm's OWN income tax, prepaid: DR WHT Receivable (an asset) in the settlement entry, the receivable's evidence being the customer's certificate. Two disciplines make the asset real: the capture (every deduction recognised as WHT at allocation — the shortpay coded correctly, the asset built transaction by transaction) and the certificate chase (the standing worklist: deductions taken, certificates outstanding, aged per customer — chased with the same professionalism as any receivable, because an uncertificated deduction is money in limbo: suffered but unprovable). The asset's destiny closes the loop: WHT suffered offsets the firm's income tax liability — the credit the accountant applies at filing — which is why the chase MATTERS in naira: every uncollected certificate is the firm's own tax paid twice, once by deduction and once at assessment.

The both-directions month. A trading firm of any size runs both lives simultaneously: deducting from its service suppliers while being deducted from by its corporate customers — two accounts (one liability, one asset), two registers, two worklists (the remittance schedule and the certificate chase), never netted (module 4's law verbatim: different assertions, different destinies). The monthly ritual runs both: agent side — register closed, tied to WHT Payable, remitted, zeroed, certificates dispatched; sufferer side — deductions captured, certificates chased, the receivable's aging read, the accountant handed the period's asset position for the CIT picture. Twenty minutes each when the disciplines hold; the alternative — both directions run on memory — is the module's most reliably expensive neglect, and Chapter 9's case study prices it in recovered naira.

lessons.title: Chapter 5 — PAYE & the payroll custodies
lessons.html:
The payroll journal (module 2) credited a row of custody accounts in one line; this chapter opens the row — the employee-money custodies, their rhythms, and the tie that keeps payroll defensible.

The custody family. The monthly payroll carves an employee's gross into destinations, and each destination is an account with an authority behind it: PAYE — the employee's income tax, withheld under the current law's bands and reliefs (the 2025 reform reshaped the bands and the low-income threshold — the accountant's living table; the system's contribution is a payroll setup that applies whatever the current structure is), remitted monthly to the STATE of the employee's residence (the multi-state workforce means multi-state remittance — a Lagos head office with Ogun-resident staff files in both, and the payroll register must split by state to serve it); pension — the contributory scheme's employee and employer portions, remitted to each employee's chosen fund administrator (plural administrators, one schedule — the register splits by PFA); and the levy family the accountant confirms applicability of by headcount and sector — housing fund, insurance trust, industrial training — each a small account with its own rhythm. The employer's OWN portions (pension employer share, the levies borne by the firm) are expense, not custody — the distinction the grammar makes automatic and the reader should hold: withheld-from-employee is custody; borne-by-employer is cost.

The payroll tie. The register-to-account bridge, payroll edition: the payroll register's column totals (gross, PAYE, pension by portion, net pay) tie to the payroll journal's lines, which tie to the custody accounts' movements, which zero at remittance — one chain, checked monthly in minutes, and the chain's health is what makes every payroll question answerable: the employee disputing a deduction (the register's row, the payslip's mirror), the authority querying a remittance (the schedule, the receipt), the auditor sampling a month (the chain, walked). The payslip discipline rides here: every employee receives the statement of their own carving — gross, deductions itemised, net — every month, because the payslip is the employee's certificate (the WHT logic, personal edition) and the firm's first defence in any deduction dispute.

The rhythms and the year. Monthly: PAYE remitted by the calendar's day (state by state), pension within its statutory window (fund by fund), the custodies zeroing after each. Annually: the employer's returns — the annual PAYE return declaring every employee's year (filed to each relevant state), and the reconciliations the accountant runs between the twelve monthly filings and the annual declaration. The system's job throughout is the register that can produce ANY slice on demand — by month, by employee, by state, by fund — because every payroll obligation is a different slice of one dataset, and a firm whose payroll lives in the system answers all of them from one place. The firm whose payroll lives in a spreadsheet beside the system answers none of them without archaeology — and reconciles the spreadsheet to the GL never, which is Chapter 10's filing-from-outside pattern wearing its most common face.

lessons.title: Chapter 6 — The filing & remittance ritual: the zeroing invariant
lessons.html:
Every custody chapter ended at the same machinery; here it is once, generalised — the monthly ritual that turns tax from anxiety into procedure, and the invariant that proves each cycle clean.

The ritual's six steps, for any custody. Close the register — the month's document-level detail (invoices for VAT, deductions for WHT, the payroll register for PAYE) cut off at the period, because the register is the return's evidence and the account's mirror. Reconcile register to account — the bridge, to the kobo, divergences worked NOW: the register-account disagreement found before filing is a bookkeeping task; found after, it is an amended return, an authority conversation, or both. Prepare the return FROM the system — the return restates the ledger; the parallel spreadsheet computation is the pattern this module keeps convicting, because two computations guarantee a divergence and the filed one wins the argument with the authority while the booked one wins it with the auditor: one source, or two problems. File by the date — the calendar's line (Chapter 7), owned by name. Remit — the payment entry, from the reserve (Chapter 7's discipline), referenced to the filing. Verify the zero — the invariant: after a clean cycle, each custody account returns to its explainable level — zero for the fully-remitted custodies, the stated carry-forward for VAT credit months — and any unexplained residue is next month's first investigation, because a custody account that will not zero is telling one of a short list of stories: a register-account divergence (the bridge skipped), a remittance short or misposted (the payment against the wrong account), a prior month's residue compounding (the drift that becomes archaeology), or custody spent (Chapter 1's disease, surfacing as arithmetic).

The evidence file. Each cycle files its bundle: the register extract, the reconciliation, the return as filed, the filing acknowledgment, the remittance evidence, the zero-verification — one folder per tax per month, boring and complete. This is Chapter 8's audit posture being built monthly as a by-product (the academy's oldest economics: the system that runs well IS the system that evidences well), and its absence is why authority queries paralyse unprepared firms: the answer exists but the assembling is a week, and a week's silence reads as evasion when a day's reply reads as competence.

The penalties frame — why late is expensive, without the rate table. The consultant's framing for owners, numbers left to the accountant: Nigerian tax penalties compound along three axes — the fixed late-filing penalties (per return, accruing monthly), interest on unremitted amounts (running from the due date), and the escalation costs (the audit attention a chronically-late filer invites, the tax clearance certificate — needed for contracts, banking, and bids — delayed or denied). The arithmetic the framing produces: the cost of the RITUAL is a few hours monthly; the cost of its absence is penalties plus interest plus the commercial doors a missing clearance closes — and the comparison is not close. Compliance's best-kept secret, taught to every client: the authorities are overwhelmingly manageable for the firm that files on time from records that tie; nearly all compliance pain concentrates on the firms that force reconstruction — and which side of that line a firm lives on is decided by this chapter's six steps, run monthly, owned by name.

lessons.title: Chapter 7 — The compliance calendar & the reserve
lessons.html:
The rituals need their WHEN and their MONEY. The consolidated calendar, and the reserve discipline that makes remittance day a transfer instead of a crisis.

The calendar, consolidated. The monthly spine — the recurring dates a trading firm lives by (the specific statutory days are the accountant's confirmation; the SHAPE is universal): the VAT return and remittance in the month's third week for the prior month; WHT remittance on its earlier track (the agent's custody moves faster — typically the third week for federal, with state-collected streams on their own days); PAYE to each relevant state by its mid-month day; pension within days of paying salaries (the tightest window in the family — statutorily pinned to the payment of wages, not the month's end). The annual layer rides above: companies income tax filing on the firm's filing horizon (months after year-end, the accountant's flagship), the annual PAYE employer returns in the new year's first month, and the levy family's annual cycles. The calendar is built ONCE per client — every obligation, its authority, its day, its OWNER, its evidence-file location — and it lives where every calendar in this academy lives: on the policy page, reviewed annually and at every legal change, with module 8 slotting it into the finance function's master rhythm.

The reserve discipline. Chapter 1 named the disease (custody spent); here is the structural cure: the tax custodies SEGREGATED in cash, not just in accounts — the tax-reserve bank account (module 3's purpose-per-account control, now with its most important tenant) receiving, on a rhythm, the cash matching the custody balances: the month's VAT position swept as it accrues or at close, the WHT deductions moved when withheld, the payroll custodies parked at payroll run. The mechanics are one contra entry per sweep (module 3's machinery); the discipline is the RULE that the reserve is not working capital — it is the state's money sitting in a room with the state's name on it — and the payoff is the module's promised boredom: remittance day is a transfer from a funded account, executed by the calendar, with no scramble, no bridging loan, and no conversation about which supplier waits so the state can be paid. The sizing honesty: firms under genuine cash strain will resist the sweep (we need that float) — and the consultant's answer is the framing that has closed this argument at every client who heard it: the custody money was never the firm's float; spending it is borrowing from the state at penalty-plus-interest rates without asking — the most expensive credit line in Nigeria, taken by default. A firm that cannot fund its reserve has a working-capital problem to solve honestly (the receivables discipline, the stock release ladder — tools three tracks supplied), not a tax float to burn.

The cash-flow read. The calendar's obligations, projected: the rolling view of what falls due in the next 60-90 days against the reserve's funding — one line on the treasury read (module 3's daily position glance, extended), and the early-warning that converts the rare genuine squeeze from a deadline-day crisis into a planned conversation (the authority approached BEFORE the due date about instalments is a different meeting than the one after — the accountant leads it; the system's contribution is that the numbers were known in time to have it).

lessons.title: Chapter 8 — Audits & the evidence posture
lessons.html:
Sooner or later the authority asks questions — the desk query, the reconciliation request, the field audit. The chair's preparation is not lawyering; it is a POSTURE, built monthly, and this chapter is its anatomy.

The posture in one sentence. Registers tied to accounts tied to documents, filed on time, evidenced in folders — when that chain exists, every authority question is an extraction exercise; when it doesn't, every question is a reconstruction project, and reconstruction under deadline is where firms concede assessments they never owed. The posture is Chapter 6's evidence file compounding: twelve monthly folders per tax per year, each self-contained, and the audit support task collapsing to which months, which taxes — here.

The encounter types, at working altitude. The desk review — the authority's routine reconciliation: their records of your filings against their expectations (increasingly automated as the e-invoicing rails mature — Chapter 2's point that they now hold half the reconciliation; the firm whose register fed its returns matches by construction, and the mismatch letters go to the firms that filed parallel computations). The query letter — specific questions on specific periods: answered ON-RECORD (module 4's dispute hygiene, authority edition — the reply in writing, the evidence attached, the file noting what was sent when), within the stated window, factually and without volunteering adjacent essays (answer what was asked, completely; the accountant reviews before it goes). The field audit — the authority in the building: the preparation is the standing posture plus logistics (a room, a liaison — ONE person through whom requests flow, so the audit gets consistent, logged responses instead of hallway answers), and the consultant's role defined precisely: produce evidence, not arguments — the system's records extracted cleanly, the drill-downs demonstrated where they help, the POSITIONS argued by the accountant and the tax adviser, never by the consultant (Chapter 2's boundary, at its highest-stakes appearance).

The common findings, pre-empted. What trading-firm audits actually find, each one a chapter of this academy running in reverse: output VAT on invoices absent from returns (the register-return divergence — the bridge skipped); input VAT claimed on defective invoices (the evidence discipline — Procurement 7's invoice-quality money lesson); WHT deducted but unremitted (the custody spent — the finding with interest attached); WHT remitted but unscheduled (the detail register absent — remittances the authority cannot attribute); PAYE understated against the payroll reality (the spreadsheet-beside-the-system disease); and related-party and cash transactions undocumented (the evidence posture's edges). The consultant reading this list correctly sees the module's rituals as the pre-emption of every line — which is the honest sales pitch for the whole module: the audit that ends early is not lucky; it is the monthly folders, met.

The posture's tone. Last, the cultural note consultants transmit to clients: the relationship with the authority is long, and the firm's reputation with it is an asset — filings on time, replies on record, positions argued professionally through the right professionals, and the tax clearance certificate renewed as the routine it becomes. Firms that treat every interaction as combat buy attention; firms that treat compliance as the subscription it is buy quiet — and quiet, for a trading firm with margins to make, is worth more than any argument ever won.

lessons.title: Chapter 9 — Case study: HealthTrade's compliance year
lessons.html:
The silent partner, professionally held. Every chapter clocks in.

The consolidation (Ch. 1, 3). The chair's first month assembles what three tracks built: the four custody accounts confirmed and typed, the item masters' tax categories audited (the pharmacy's exempt basic-medicine lines vs standard-rated cosmetics — 14 items re-categorised, the mixed-supply registers now able to tell their streams apart, the apportionment question handed to the accountant WITH clean data), and the first full monthly VAT ritual run end to end: registers closed, both bridges tied to the kobo, the return prepared from the system, filed, remitted from the new reserve, VAT Payable verified at zero. The accountant's note in the file: first month the return and the ledger were the same document.

The certificate chase (Ch. 4). The WHT Receivable archaeology: the sufferer-side register reconstructed from allocation history finds ₦1.34m of deductions suffered over two years — certificates held for only ₦610k. The chase instituted: outstanding certificates listed per customer, aged, worked like receivables (the corporate customers' finance teams contacted with the professional ask; the government customer escalated through its due process) — eight months later, certificates for a further ₦590k recovered and handed to the accountant for the CIT credit: the firm's own tax, un-paid-twice, at the cost of a standing worklist. The remaining ₦140k — deductions by two defunct customers, certificates unobtainable — is written to the accountant's judgment with its file: even the loss is now a documented decision instead of a quiet leak.

The reserve's first test (Ch. 7). Month four: a heavy import quarter squeezes cash, and the old instinct surfaces in a management meeting — the VAT account has ₦2.1m sitting idle; borrow it for the Emzor payment, replace it by the 21st. The framing does its work: the custody argument restated (the most expensive credit line in Nigeria, taken by default), the ALTERNATIVE worked instead — module 4's receivables push accelerates two collections; the stock ladder releases a slow line — and the reserve stays whole. Remittance day passes as a transfer, as designed; and the MD's conversion is complete by Q3, when the reserve sweep becomes the month's first standing transfer rather than its last argument.

The desk query (Ch. 8). Month nine: a query letter — two months' VAT, the authority's e-invoice-fed expectation against the filed returns, one difference flagged. The evidence posture answers it in a day: the difference traced in the file to a credit note issued in month six (reducing output legitimately — the document, the register line, the return's treatment all agreeing), the reply drafted on-record with the evidence attached, the accountant's review, sent within the window. The authority's closure letter arrives in three weeks; the file gains its first external validation; and the office learns the lesson at the right price: the folder answered before we finished worrying.

The transition navigated (Ch. 2, 5). Across the year, the reform's working edges land as calendar items, not crises: the payroll setup re-based when the accountant confirms the new PAYE structure (the system applying the current bands the day they take effect; the multi-state split — Lagos and Ogun — running from the register's state column), the small-company eligibility question answered by the accountant with the system's turnover read as evidence, and the e-invoicing rail's expansion absorbed by a firm whose invoices already fed its returns. The year closes with the compliance calendar's every line green, the twelve monthly folders complete, the clearance certificate renewed routinely — and the module's cultural argument won in the accountant's year-end words: tax used to be the thing we feared quarterly; now it's the thing we do monthly.

lessons.title: Chapter 10 — Common mistakes & the fifth law
lessons.html:
The tax layer's scar tissue — each pattern a firm somewhere is living right now. Symptom → disease → fix.

Pattern 1 — custody spent. Symptom: remittance day as recurring crisis; the VAT account funded by scramble; interest and penalties as line items. Disease: the state's money used as float (Ch. 1, 7) — the most expensive credit line in Nigeria, taken by default. Fix: the reserve account with its sweep rhythm, the working-capital problem solved honestly with the academy's real tools, and the custody framing taught until it holds.

Pattern 2 — the parallel computation. Symptom: returns prepared in spreadsheets beside the system; the filed numbers and the booked numbers diverging; nobody able to say which is true. Disease: two sources (Ch. 6) — the return no longer a restatement of the ledger. Fix: the return FROM the system, the registers' bridges as the pre-filing gate, and the spreadsheet retired to what it should be — a formatting tool, never a source.

Pattern 3 — the unreconciled registers. Symptom: register totals and account movements that drift apart unexamined; the desk review's mismatch letter arriving as a surprise. Disease: the bridges skipped (Ch. 3, 6) — while the authority's e-invoice rails now run their half automatically. Fix: the register-to-account line in every monthly ritual, divergences worked before filing, and the zeroing invariant verified as each cycle's close.

Pattern 4 — certificates uncollected. Symptom: WHT suffered for years with a certificate file that fits in an envelope; the CIT bill paid gross. Disease: the sufferer side run on resignation (Ch. 4) — the firm's own tax paid twice, quietly. Fix: the deduction captured at allocation, the chase as a standing aged worklist, and the recovered credits handed to the accountant with their evidence — the module's most reliably fundable ritual.

Pattern 5 — payroll beside the system. Symptom: salaries in a spreadsheet, a monthly lump journal, PAYE computed elsewhere, state splits improvised, the annual return an archaeology project. Disease: the register that can produce any slice replaced by one that produces none (Ch. 5). Fix: payroll into the system (or rigorously bridged), the custody chain checked monthly, payslips as the standing employee certificate, and the annual return reduced to an extract.

Pattern 6 — penalties as a cost of doing business. Symptom: chronic lateness normalised; the clearance certificate perpetually delayed; the authority's attention earned and compounding. Disease: the calendar unowned (Ch. 6-7) — compliance experienced as weather instead of run as a rhythm. Fix: the consolidated calendar with names, the reserve making funding a non-event, and the cultural reset the case study modelled — from feared quarterly to done monthly.

The fifth law. The chart is the language; the journal is the exception; the bank is the outside witness; the controls tie or nothing is trusted. The fifth names the silent partner's terms: tax accounts are custody, not cost — the state's money is held in its own accounts, reconciled to its registers, remitted on the calendar, and evidenced forever. Both VAT sides joined monthly, both WHT directions worked, the payroll chain tied, the six-step ritual zeroing every custody, the reserve keeping the money where the name is, and the evidence file answering every question in a day. Module 6 turns from what the firm owes to where the firm earns: cost centers and dimensions — the machinery that gives profit an address.

dimensions.title: Accounts 6 — Cost Centers & Dimensions
dimensions.desc: Profit gets an address: the one-chart-many-lenses thesis, the cost center tree shadowing accountability, the address cascade and mandatory validation, the branch P&L on contribution, the allocation doctrine, budgets vs actuals, and the second dimension for service lines and projects.

lessons.title: Chapter 1 — Profit has an address
lessons.html:
Module 1 planted the seed in one sentence — the chart answers WHAT KIND of money; dimensions answer WHOSE and WHERE — and deferred the harvest here. This module is the harvest: the machinery that lets one firm read many profits — per branch, per service line, per project — without the chart ever learning their names.

The question this module answers. Every owner of a multi-branch or multi-line firm asks it, usually in the first meeting: which branch actually makes money? The unstructured answer is folklore (the flagship 'carries' the network; the new branch 'must be losing'; the service side 'pays for itself' — all asserted, none known). The structured answer requires that every naira of revenue and cost carries, from the moment it posts, an ADDRESS — the branch, the line, the project it belongs to — so that the P&L can be filtered by address and read true. That address is the dimension, and the module's thesis is the design law that governs it: one chart, many lenses — the chart stays a single language (Rent is one account, everywhere), and the dimensions multiply the READINGS of it (Rent at Ibadan, Rent at Akure) without multiplying the words.

The disease this module prevents. The alternative design — met constantly in the wild — is the per-branch chart copy: Rent - Ibadan, Rent - Akure, Rent - HQ, and so on for every expense, every branch: three branches turning a 60-line P&L structure into 180 accounts, five branches into 300, with every new branch a chart surgery, every firm-wide read a manual re-addition of scattered leaves, and every posting a navigation exercise through near-identical names (the mis-post rate rising with the count). Module 1 named it chart sprawl's worst species; this module supplies the cure it promised: the branch belongs in the DIMENSION field, entered once, cascading by default (Chapter 3), and the chart never grows when the firm does — the test of the design being exactly that: opening branch four should touch the dimension list and not one account.

What dimensions are NOT. Three boundary stakes before the machinery: dimensions are not a second chart (they carry no balances of their own — they are tags on GL entries, and every dimensional read is the same GL filtered); they are not only for the P&L (balance-sheet dimensioning exists and has uses, but the module's centre of gravity is where the commercial questions live — revenue and cost); and they are not free (every mandatory dimension is a field someone fills on every posting forever — the reading test of module 1 applies with full force: a dimension earns existence when someone will READ its cut separately and act on it, and Chapter 7 polices the sprawl). The module's shape follows the address's life: the address book (Chapter 2), the writing of addresses (Chapter 3), the reading of them (Chapters 4-6), the second dimension (Chapter 7), and the law (Chapter 9).

lessons.title: Chapter 2 — Cost centers: the address book
lessons.html:
The primary dimension has a name and a structure: the cost center — and its design hour is the third tree this academy has taught you to plant. The same laws, the new ground.

The tree, again. Cost centers form a tree: GROUP cost centers for rollup reading (Branches; Operations), LEAF cost centers that take postings (Ibadan Branch; Akure Branch; Head Office) — postings to groups refused by the design (the third appearance of the law: money exists at leaves; groups exist so leaves can be read together), and the company's tree rooted at a main cost center that anchors the whole. Every warehouse-tree and chart-tree discipline transfers untouched: named for the decade, shallow (two levels below root serves almost every trading firm), designed from what must be read, changed as events, retired never deleted.

Designing the address book. The design question is WHOSE performance the firm manages — and the answer is the accountability structure, not the org chart's vanity: a leaf per unit that has an OWNER and a P&L conversation (each branch — a manager answers for it; head office — the shared-function home Chapter 5 will allocate from; the warehouse/distribution operation where it is managed as its own unit), and NOT a leaf per department that exists only on paper, per team of two, or per activity nobody reviews separately (the reading test, again — a cost center nobody's monthly conversation names is sprawl wearing a lanyard). The parallel that makes design fast: the cost center tree usually SHADOWS the warehouse tree's accountability layer (Inventory 1's custodians are frequently this module's P&L owners), and where the two diverge, the divergence should be explainable in one sentence or it is a mistake in one tree or the other.

The default machinery. The company carries a default cost center (the unaddressed posting's fallback — and Chapter 3 argues the fallback should almost never fire); masters carry theirs (the warehouse or branch record wired to its cost center; item groups where product-line reading matters; users where the operator IS the address — the till assistant whose every posting belongs to their branch). The defaults do the labour: a well-wired firm addresses ninety-something percent of its postings without anyone touching the field, which is the design goal — the address written by architecture, corrected by exception.

Cost centers vs the second dimension, previewed. One structural note before the wiring chapter: the cost center is the PRIMARY lens (branch/unit accountability — every firm needs it), and the system's accounting-dimension machinery allows FURTHER lenses beside it (service line, project — Chapter 7's terrain) that cut ACROSS branches rather than within them: the clinic service line exists at two branches; the branch and the line are different questions about the same naira, carried in different fields. The design discipline is not to conflate them — the cost center tree that tries to be branch-times-line (Ibadan-Retail, Ibadan-Clinic, Akure-Retail...) is rebuilding the per-branch chart copy one level down, multiplying leaves geometrically where two independent dimensions would multiply them not at all. Two questions, two fields — the module's quiet design gem, and the one that saves the most cleanup engagements.

lessons.title: Chapter 3 — Wiring the address into every posting
lessons.html:
An address book is useless if letters go unaddressed. This chapter is the wiring: where the dimension gets written, how the defaults cascade, and the validation that makes the address a law instead of a hope.

Where the address is written. Every P&L-touching document carries the field, and the granularity matters: header-level (the whole document one address — the branch invoice, the branch expense) and row-level (each line its own — the head-office purchase that splits across branches, the invoice mixing service lines), with row overriding header, because real documents mix addresses more often than design imagines. The posting map (module 1) gains its dimension column: the sales invoice's income line carries the selling branch (cascaded from the till, the warehouse, or the user); the delivery's COGS carries the same (the stock came from the branch's leaf — the warehouse-to-cost-center wiring doing the work); the purchase invoice's expense lines carry their consumers (row-level where the consumption splits); the journal's rows carry theirs (module 2's anatomy already demanded it — the expense journal that charges without addressing is the letter posted blank); payroll carries the employee's unit (the register's dimension column — module 5's payroll journal, now with addresses).

The cascade. Defaults resolve in a sensible order — the specific beats the general: the row's explicit entry beats the header's, the header's beats the master-derived default (the item group's, the warehouse's, the customer's where wired), the master's beats the user's, and the user's beats the company fallback. The consultant's wiring hour sets this cascade so the FRONT LINE almost never sees the field: the Ibadan till user's sales land at Ibadan because the user and warehouse both say so; the Akure expense claim lands at Akure because the claimant does; and the field surfaces for human decision only where the machine genuinely cannot know — the shared purchase, the split service — which is exactly where a human SHOULD decide.

Validation: the address as law. The system's dimension-validation machinery closes the gap between mostly-addressed and always-addressed: dimensions marked MANDATORY for the account ranges that need them (all income and expense accounts, at minimum — the P&L posting that cannot save without its address is the design working; balance-sheet ranges per the firm's reading needs), with the company fallback thereby demoted from silent catch-all to visible exception. The conviction underneath: an OPTIONAL address decays — the first busy week writes blanks, the blanks accumulate in the default cost center, and six months later the branch P&L carries an 'unaddressed' lump that quietly absorbs whatever made it inconvenient — the suspense-account disease (module 1) in dimensional clothes, cured the same way: the lump swept monthly to its true addresses while it is small, and the validation tightened so it stops refilling.

Retrofits, honestly priced. The wiring installed at go-live costs a design hour; retrofitted after a year of unaddressed trading it costs an engagement — history cannot be re-addressed wholesale (the entries stand; the addresses were never captured), so the retrofit draws a line (dimensional truth from the cutover forward, the prior period read only at firm level) and the consultant prices the difference plainly to every prospect who asks for branch P&Ls 'from our existing data': the data has no addresses; the future can. One more instance of the academy's oldest pricing law: architecture at setup is cheap; archaeology is not.

lessons.title: Chapter 4 — The branch P&L: the payoff read
lessons.html:
The addresses exist so this page can: the branch P&L — the owner's first-meeting question, answered monthly, honestly. The read, and the honesty rules that keep it meaning something.

The natural half: revenue and direct cost. Filtered by the branch's cost center, the P&L's top assembles itself from the wiring: revenue by branch (every sale carried its source), COGS by branch (the delivery's valuation release carried it too — Inventory 5's machinery now readable per room), and the branch's DIRECT expenses (its rent, its payroll, its power, its local running costs — each posted with its address at entry). This much is arithmetic, and its honesty is exactly the wiring's honesty: a branch P&L is as true as Chapter 3's validation kept it, which is why the unaddressed-lump sweep precedes every monthly read.

The harder half: shared costs. Head office exists — the MD's salary, the accountant, the shared warehouse, the group marketing, this system's own subscription — and none of it posted to a branch because none of it belongs to one. The design question with teeth: SHOULD it appear on branch P&Ls at all? Chapter 5 holds the allocation doctrine; this chapter holds the reading frame that makes the doctrine usable: contribution before net. The contribution view — branch revenue minus branch COGS minus branch direct costs — answers the operational question (does this branch, as a trading unit, generate surplus?) with numbers that are all FACTS: everything on the page posted where it happened, nothing estimated, nothing arguable. The fully-loaded view — contribution minus an allocated share of head office — answers a different question (does the branch cover its share of existing overheads?) with numbers that are part fact, part POLICY (the allocation basis is a choice), and the reading discipline is to keep the two views SEPARATE and labelled: contribution is the branch manager's page (they control everything on it); the loaded view is the owner's portfolio page (worth seeing, dangerous to act on alone).

The classic misread, pre-empted. The fully-loaded view's danger deserves its own paragraph because it closes branches that shouldn't close: the newest or smallest branch shows a fully-loaded loss (its allocated overhead share swamps its young contribution), someone proposes closing it — and the arithmetic they are missing is that closing it deletes the CONTRIBUTION while the allocated overheads (the MD, the accountant, the head office rent) survive entirely, landing on the remaining branches: the network is poorer by exactly the closed branch's positive contribution, and the next-smallest branch now looks worse by its inherited share — the death spiral of allocation-led decisions, walked one branch at a time. The rule the consultant teaches with this parable: close on contribution, expand on contribution, and use the loaded view only to size the overhead conversation itself (is head office too heavy for this network? — a real question, aimed at the right object).

The branch P&L's rhythm. Monthly, per branch, contribution format, pushed TO the branch manager (Inventory 6's pushed-scorecard law — the page they see moves behaviour), with the branch's stock-health vitals beside it where the firm runs the full academy stack (the two pages sharing a room: the branch that reads its P&L and its stock page together is managing a business, not a shop). The network rollup — branches side by side, contribution ranked, trends marked — is the owner's monthly page, and module 7 will seat both in the close.

lessons.title: Chapter 5 — Allocating shared costs: the doctrine
lessons.html:
The residue of costs that genuinely serve everyone must either stay unallocated (honest, but leaves the loaded view unbuilt) or be shared by rule. The allocation doctrine — brief, written, and deliberately boring.

Direct first, always. The doctrine's first rule shrinks the problem before sharing it: everything attributable at SOURCE is posted there and never enters allocation — the group marketing campaign that ran for one branch's opening (that branch's), the head-office staffer seconded to a project (the project's — Chapter 7), the shared warehouse's costs where the warehouse serves branches measurably (the distribution cost-center reading, recharged by throughput if the firm wants that precision). Every naira attributed directly is a naira the allocation argument never touches, and mature firms allocate a RESIDUE, not a bloc: the smaller the allocated pool, the smaller the fiction, the quieter Chapter 5's wars.

Bases for the residue. What remains — genuinely joint costs — shares by a WRITTEN basis chosen per cost family for rough fairness and, above all, stability: revenue share (the default for general overheads — simple, proportional to activity, gameable by nothing the branches control improperly), headcount (for people-driven costs — HR, welfare, training), space (for premises-driven costs where premises are shared), and throughput (for the distribution recharge where measured). The numbers matter less than three properties: the basis is WRITTEN (the policy page — every allocation question answered by pointing, not arguing), STABLE (changed annually at most, as an event with a memo — a basis that moves monthly is a dial, and module 4's provision conviction applies verbatim: movements should mean something), and VISIBLE (allocated lines shown AS allocated on the loaded view — labelled, separable, never blended into direct costs, so any reader can reconstruct contribution by covering one section with a thumb).

The allocation wars, and their treaty. Where allocation is argued monthly, the pattern is always the same: the basis is unwritten or unstable, the allocated pool is too large (direct-first neglected), and the loaded view is being used for decisions it cannot carry (Chapter 4's misread institutionalised — branch bonuses on loaded profit is the classic accelerant, converting an accounting convention into a compensation fight). The treaty is the doctrine itself: shrink the pool, write the basis, freeze it annually, label the lines, and move the incentive conversation to contribution and the vitals the manager actually controls — after which the allocation becomes what it should have been all along: a footnote that sizes the overhead conversation, read quarterly by the owner, argued by no one.

What not to allocate. The doctrine's last fence: costs that are POLICY rather than operations — the owner's discretionary spends, the group's expansion bets, financing costs of decisions branches didn't make — sit best at head office unallocated, because pushing them down teaches branch managers to argue about naira they cannot influence, which is the exact opposite of what the address system exists to produce: pages where every line is someone's to move. The one-sentence summary the consultant leaves behind: allocate little, allocate by writing, and never let an allocated naira outvote a contributed one.

lessons.title: Chapter 6 — Budgets vs actuals: the forward address
lessons.html:
Dimensions address the past; budgets address the future — and the machinery joins them: the budget set per cost center and account, the actuals landing beside it, and the monthly variance read that turns the pair into management. The forward half of the address system.

The budget machinery. Budgets attach where the reading lives: per cost center (the branch's expense budget, head office's own), per account (or account group), per fiscal year with monthly or periodic distribution (the even split for steady costs; the seasonal curve for the trade that has one — the December-heavy retail budget that expects its own Q4). The system holds the budget beside the actuals it accumulates, and the variance — actual against budget, by address, by account, by month and cumulatively — becomes a standing read rather than a spreadsheet reunion. The control machinery rides where wanted: budget ACTIONS on exceeding (warn, or stop — the hard stop reserved for the account families where overspend is governance failure rather than trading reality, because a stop on COGS in a good sales month is the machinery fighting the business).

Building budgets that mean something. The consultant's contribution to budget QUALITY is structural: budgets built per address from that address's OWN history (the branch's last-year actuals as the base — the system supplies them by construction, which is the address system paying its first forward dividend), adjusted by known changes (the new branch's ramp, the rent review, the headcount plan), owned by the address's owner (the branch manager who built their number defends it differently than one who received it — the budget conversation is the accountability structure exercising), and approved as a set (the rollup must reconcile to the firm's plan — branch ambitions summing to more than the network's cash is a conversation to have in November, not discover in March).

The variance read. Monthly, by address, the discipline is CAUSE before comment: a variance decomposes (volume vs rate — sold more units, or spent more per unit; timing vs level — the cost that moved months, or the cost that grew; one-off vs run-rate — the repair that happened, or the drift that will repeat), and the read's output is the same shape as every read this academy has built: the material variances each carrying a one-line story and an owner, the immaterial noise left alone (variance thresholds set so the meeting discusses six lines, not sixty), and the aggregate trend watched (the branch consistently 10% over on one line has a budget error or a control gap — the read tells you to find out which). The framing that keeps budgets healthy: the budget is a conversation instrument, not a straitjacket — its job is to make the difference between plan and reality DISCUSSABLE early, and a firm that punishes every variance teaches its managers to budget slack and hide news, which kills the instrument to win the meeting.

Budget theatre, named early. The failure mode Chapter 9 will convict, previewed because prevention is cheap: budgets built once, filed, and consulted at year-end to explain what already happened — the instrument as decoration. The tell is the variance read's absence from the monthly rhythm; the fix is the seat module 7 reserves for it in the close — and the honest sizing note that budgets are the address system's OPTIONAL layer: a small firm may run addresses and contribution reads for a year before budgeting formally, and that sequence is sound; theatre is not a stage of maturity, it is its counterfeit.

lessons.title: Chapter 7 — Projects & service lines: the second dimension
lessons.html:
The cost center answered WHERE; some firms need a second question answered — WHAT LINE, WHICH JOB — and the accounting-dimension machinery carries it. The second lens, and the governance that keeps lenses from multiplying into fog.

When a dimension earns existence. The reading test, at its sternest, because every mandatory dimension taxes every posting forever: a second dimension earns its field when (all three) someone will READ its cut monthly and act on it, the cut crosses the first dimension (the service line that exists at several branches — if it nests inside one branch, the cost center tree already carries it), and the postings can be attributed at entry with reasonable defaults (a dimension the front line cannot fill truthfully fills falsely — the address system's honesty is only ever the entry moment's honesty). Two dimensions serve almost every trading firm that needs any; the third is rare and argued hard; the fourth is fog.

The service-line lens. The mixed firm's standing need — the pharmacy with a clinic corner, the retailer with an installation arm, the distributor with a logistics-for-hire side: one branch, two businesses, and the branch P&L alone cannot say which one earns. The service-line dimension cuts the same GL the other way: revenue by line (the invoice rows carry it — item-group defaults doing the cascade: clinic services default to Clinic, shop items to Retail), direct costs by line (the clinic's pharmacist, its consumables), and the two-way read the pair of dimensions unlocks — the branch-by-line matrix (Ibadan's clinic vs Akure's clinic; each branch's retail core) that answers expansion's real questions: not should we add clinics but the clinic line contributes X at Ibadan and Y at Akure — what differs, and which model travels. Contribution framing governs here exactly as in Chapter 4, and shared-within-branch costs (the premises both lines sit in) allocate by the same doctrine or, better, stay at the branch's shared level unallocated — the fences transfer whole.

The project lens. The job-shaped work — the fit-out contract, the installation project, the one-off supply tender — wants its own cut: revenue, costs, and hence margin PER JOB, opened when the job opens and closed when it closes (the dimension value with a lifecycle — unlike branches and lines, projects END, and the value list needs its retirement discipline: completed projects closed to new postings, their read archived, the list kept short and living). The project dimension is where mixed trading-and-jobs firms discover their jobs' truth — the tender that won on price and lost on margin becomes visible per job instead of dissolving into the year's blended result — and the discipline that makes it work is entry-moment attribution: the job's purchases addressed to it at the purchase, the job's hours (where tracked) at the timesheet, because a project P&L reconstructed at job's end from memory is a negotiation, not a reading.

Dimension hygiene. The value lists are MASTERS and get master governance (the item-master laws, fourth appearance): values created by the named owner only (dimension sprawl is chart sprawl's second cousin — the 'Misc' service line, the duplicate project, the test value that lived), named to convention, retired by lifecycle, and audited annually beside the chart walk. And the validation discipline mirrors Chapter 3: mandatory where the reading demands it, defaulted where the cascade can know, surfaced for humans only at genuine forks — the same architecture-writes-most-addresses goal, applied to every lens the firm runs.

lessons.title: Chapter 8 — Case study: HealthTrade's addresses
lessons.html:
The address system, installed and read. Every chapter clocks in.

The tree and the wiring (Ch. 2-3). The design hour with the MD and accountant: four leaves under two groups — Branches (Central/Lagos, Ibadan, Akure) and Head Office — shadowing the warehouse tree's accountability layer exactly (the one divergence, the shared distribution operation, gets its own leaf with a one-sentence justification: it is managed as a unit and will be read as one). Defaults cascade from warehouses and users; income and expense accounts get mandatory validation; the posting map is re-verified with its new dimension column (one live document per kind, addresses read aloud — the go-live hour's second edition). Month one's unaddressed lump: ₦0 — the validation refused every blank at birth.

The first branch P&L, and the MD's lesson (Ch. 4). Month two's read, contribution format, three branches side by side: Central contributes strongly, Ibadan solidly — and Akure, eight months old, contributes ₦310,000... which the fully-loaded view (head office allocated by revenue share) turns into a ₦140,000 'loss'. The MD's first instinct is the classic — Akure isn't working — and the consultant walks the parable at the whiteboard: close Akure and its ₦310k contribution leaves the network; the allocated overhead stays and re-lands on Central and Ibadan; the firm is ₦310k a month poorer and the loaded view now frowns at Ibadan. The lesson lands as the rule: close on contribution, expand on contribution — and Akure, read rightly (contribution positive at month eight, trending with the day-90 velocity findings from Inventory 6), is a young branch WORKING, not a loss. The loaded view keeps its real job: it sizes the head-office conversation, which produces one genuine action — the group's software and admin stack is renegotiated, head office lightens 8%, and every branch's loaded view improves without a single allocation argument.

The policy settles an argument (Ch. 5). Month four: the Ibadan manager disputes the marketing allocation — a campaign 'that only helped Lagos'. The policy page answers by pointing: campaign costs attributable to a branch post DIRECT (the rule's first line — and this one, on inspection, was indeed Lagos-specific: mis-posted to the shared pool, corrected by doctrine to Central's direct costs); the residue shares by revenue, annually frozen. The argument dies in four minutes, both sides satisfied — the manager because direct-first vindicated the complaint, the accountant because the policy, not the volume, decided it. The allocation pool, audited after, shrinks 22% as more spends prove attributable — the doctrine working exactly as written: allocate little.

The budget cycle (Ch. 6). Year two's budgets are built per address from each address's own year-one actuals — branch managers drafting their numbers, the rollup reconciled in November (Akure's ambitious draft trimmed against the network's cash plan, with the reasoning shared), monthly variance reads instituted at thresholds that surface six lines, not sixty. Q1's read catches one real story: Ibadan's power costs running 18% over — decomposed (rate, not volume: the generator's diesel price moved), re-forecast, and the finding handed to procurement (a bulk diesel arrangement — the address system writing letters to the buying function, the academy's loops linking).

The second dimension (Ch. 7). Month nine: the clinic corner at Central has grown into a real line, and the service-line dimension earns its existence against all three tests (read monthly, crosses branches once Ibadan's clinic opens, attributable by item-group cascade). Wired in an afternoon — clinic item groups default to Clinic, everything else to Retail — the first line read splits Central's contribution: retail strong, clinic modest but growing, staffed rightly for its stage. When Ibadan's clinic opens in Q4, the branch-by-line matrix answers the expansion question with numbers where folklore used to live: the clinic model travels, and the board minute says so citing the matrix. The MD's year-end summary is the module's thesis returned: we used to have one profit and many opinions; now we have many profits and fewer arguments.

lessons.title: Chapter 9 — Common mistakes & the sixth law
lessons.html:
The address layer's scar tissue. Symptom → disease → fix.

Pattern 1 — the per-branch chart copy. Symptom: Rent-Ibadan, Rent-Akure, Rent-HQ... hundreds of accounts, chart surgery at every opening, firm-wide reads assembled by hand. Disease: the address written into the language (Ch. 1) — dimensions unknown or distrusted at setup. Fix: the migration engagement — dimensions wired, the copies merged to single accounts by documented entries (history preserved), validation installed, and the chart returned to one language; priced honestly as the archaeology it is.

Pattern 2 — the unaddressed lump. Symptom: a default cost center absorbing a growing share of the P&L; branch reads that everyone quietly distrusts. Disease: the optional address decaying (Ch. 3) — blanks accumulating where validation should have refused them. Fix: the lump swept to true addresses while small, mandatory validation on P&L ranges, the cascade tightened so the field almost never surfaces — and the monthly sweep retained as the standing hygiene line.

Pattern 3 — allocation wars. Symptom: monthly arguments about shared-cost shares; bonuses fought over loaded profit; the basis renegotiated by whoever shouts. Disease: the doctrine absent (Ch. 5) — pool too large, basis unwritten, loaded view overloaded with decisions it cannot carry. Fix: direct-first shrinking the pool, the written basis frozen annually, labelled and separable lines, incentives moved to contribution — the treaty, installed and pointed at.

Pattern 4 — the death-spiral close. Symptom: the smallest branch closed on its loaded loss; the network poorer; the next branch now 'losing'. Disease: allocation-led decisions (Ch. 4) — the misread institutionalised. Fix: the parable taught before it is needed, contribution enthroned for open/close/expand calls, and the loaded view returned to its one job: sizing the overhead conversation.

Pattern 5 — budget theatre. Symptom: budgets built in January, cited in December, absent in between; managers budgeting slack and hiding news. Disease: the instrument as decoration, or as punishment (Ch. 6) — either kills the conversation it exists to create. Fix: the monthly variance read seated in the close, thresholds that surface stories not noise, causes before comments — and the culture reset that variances are for discussing early, not punishing late.

Pattern 6 — dimension sprawl. Symptom: four mandatory dimensions, half-filled; value lists full of Misc, duplicates, and dead projects; entry friction breeding false addresses. Disease: lenses multiplied past the reading (Ch. 7) — the fog that discredits the whole system. Fix: the reading test applied ruthlessly (two dimensions serve almost everyone), value lists governed as masters with lifecycles, and the annual dimension audit beside the chart walk.

The sixth law. The chart is the language; the journal is the exception; the bank is the outside witness; the controls tie; tax accounts are custody. The sixth gives every naira its address: profit has an address — one chart, many lenses; every P&L posting carries its address at entry, shared costs allocate small by written policy, decisions ride contribution, and the lenses are designed like the chart: from what must be read. The tree shadows accountability, the cascade writes most addresses by architecture, the validation refuses the blank, the branch page runs on contribution, and the second dimension waits until it earns its field. Module 7 assembles everything the track has built into its destination: the period close, and the statements that are the whole system's testimony.
